newsitem.title: KENYA: Burundi army says it killed 50 rebels.
newsitem.headline: Burundi army says it killed 50 rebels.

text.p: The Burundian army said on Tuesday its troops killed 50 Hutu rebels in fighting south of the capital Bujumbura on Friday in which two of its soldiers were also killed.
Army spokesman Isaie Nibizi said by telephone the army also seized 13 weapons on Friday in Muhuta area, 27 km (17 miles) south of the capital. There was no independent confirmation of the report.

More than 150,000 people have been killed in massacres and civil war between Hutu rebels and the Tutsi-dominated army since the killing of Burundi's first freely elected Hutu president in October 1993.
Burundi's minister of the interior and public security meanwhile released a list of eight people arrested accused of involvement in a plot to assassinate military ruler Pierre Buyoya.

Burundian radio named five of them as members or officials in the Parena party, which is led by former military ruler Jean-Baptiste Bagaza. Two others were Burundian soldiers and the last was a Rwandan army deserter, state-run Burundi radio said.

Bagaza, a leading hardline Tutsi critic of Buyoya, has been under house arrest since January. Buyoya ousted Bagaza from power in 1987 and last July seized power in an army coup from a Hutu civilian president.
Regional states imposed sanctions on Burundi shortly after the coup demanding unconditional talks between the government and rebels led by Hutu guerrilla leader Leonard Nyangoma.
The plot, which authorities said they foiled last Wednesday, was the first reported against Buyoya since he took over in July.
